messages.subject_clean: Basic equating of GRM pre- and posttest
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I'm having trouble understanding the multiplegroup function. In my study I had around n=100 students going through a pretest and intervention and a posttest. But pretest and posttest were not identical. pretest consists of 5 items, posttest of 7 items, two of them are common items. all items are polytomous with different number of levels. How do I set up a multiplegroup function to get this situation, and in the end, get the correct factor scores for pre and posttest for each student?

I've been crawling through literature for 2 days now without finding a good and clear example of how to do this, although in this group I found many hints, that it should be quite easy with the mirt package and multigroup.

I would be really glad to have a generic example for my (I think rather common) case. Thanks a lot to everybody who can support me!

Kindly, Martin

messages.subject: Re: ItemPlot interpretation
messages.body_plain:
It looks like woman with low levels of worry choose answer category 1. The probability of choosing answer 1 decreases as theta rises and is and is around 50% at theta level 0 (average level of worries). Around theta level of 0  there is about  20% chance of choosing answer category 2 or 3.  However, answer 4 has about 50% chance of being chosen with theta level 0 or higher.

I would say that this item  seems more a dichotomous item than a Likert item in favour of answer 1 and  4? Consider collapsing item response categories.  Answers 2 or 3 don’t differentiatie enough between theta levels. Check the frequencies of the response categories.

The two groups of woman dont seem to differ much in their probabilities of choosing answer categories relative to theta.

Hope this helps.

Cheers Guido
